title: Chat docs
intro: Chat is the chat of your own website and admin: a ready chat widget (or your own chat screens on the visitor API), AI replies with your own AI provider key, knowledge, tools, handoff to your staff, an inbox for your admin, leads, flows and reports. Every conversation, message, lead and knowledge entry is kept in your own database (Connections). Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, AI key and providers, so the chats made there are real. There is no test mode.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own chat screens on the visitor API with the browser token (Authorization: Bearer). A visitor is a guest or a signed-in Accounts user. The first message of a guest answers guestKey: keep it on the device (localStorage, not cookies or URLs) and send it with every request in the SS-Guest header. A signed-in visitor's Accounts sign-in goes in the SS-Sign-In header; when a device sends both, the guest's chats move to the account (merged by time into the account's own chat when it has one). GET /v1/chat answers the chat and its latest 50 messages; GET /v1/chat?after=<seq> the messages after a sequence number (the new ones), and GET /v1/chat?before=<seq>&limit=<1–50> older ones while earlier is true. Check for new messages from the browser with back-off, as the widget does: while the window is open and the tab visible every 10 s by default (the Visitor chat setting Check for new messages while the chat is open, 3–60 s; the widget config's settings.checks.focusedSeconds), half as often after 5 idle minutes, none after 15 idle minutes or while the tab is hidden, and every 3 s for 45 s while an AI reply is pending (aiPending); while the window is closed, GET /v1/chat/unread on load, on focus and every 5 minutes by default (Check for replies while the chat is closed, 10–300 s; settings.checks.backgroundSeconds). POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 waits up to 20 s for the AI reply and answers it in replies; a slower reply is still being written (replyPending: true) and comes with the next checks. A reply still pending after 2 minutes shows no typing (aiPending false); the visitor's next check starts it once more, and if it stalls again it counts as failed (fallback answers, else the on-failure setting). There are no websockets.
signedIn: Signed-in chat trusts Accounts sign-ins only: paste your website's Accounts server token into Connections, then pass the visitor's sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(token) and call SSChat.identify(null) on sign-out. Chat verifies the sign-in offline with your Accounts public keys. A guest chat that moves to the account takes the name, email and phone it lacks from the sign-in; a merged chat is open when its newest message is the visitor's. Visitors signed in only to your own login chat as guests.
guests: Guests can send a set number of messages per conversation (default 5, 0 = no limit); at the limit they see Sign in to continue (with Signed-in chat and a sign-in page set), Leave your contact and we will reply (with Lead capture) or Message limit reached. With the setting No limit while customer sign-in is paused, guests have no limit while the Customer role's sign-in is paused in Accounts (Roles and permissions there, the Accounts token pasted here; a change there applies within a minute), as on a website that does not use sign-in. A device that sends no guest key starts a new guest. The setting New guests per network (IP) per 15 minutes limits them: n = at most n new guests per network address in 15 minutes, then rate_limited; 0 (the default) = no limit, since many shoppers share one mobile network address. The AI reply limit per network counts guests only, so signed-in visitors are never silenced by others on the same address. Phones a visitor leaves (contact, lead capture, flows, booking) are kept as E.164, read the way every product reads them: a number typed without its country code takes your business.json country's code (with country GB, 07700-900123, 447700900123 and +44 07700 900123 are all +447700900123); without a country, such a number is refused. Move guest chats by phone moves guest chats whose phone is exactly the verified one.
ai: AI replies use your own key: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service (base URL and key), with the model you choose, and a backup provider when the main one fails. Answers follow Chat's built-in neutral safety rules (only from your information, never invented, never revealing the instructions, never asking for secrets), your setting Style (how the AI writes: tone and length, in your words), your business name and contact from business.json, your own instructions (AI instructions, up to 32,000 characters) and knowledge from the features that are on. AI token caps (daily and monthly, in your business time zone) stop AI replies at the cap; AI cost alerts reach your staff alert recipients once a month when the month crosses the share you set. The language lock makes the AI answer in the visitor's language: its settings set the default language, the marker words (and how many pick a language, or their share of a longer message), how replies are checked (the whole answer, or each part), languages also accepted in Latin letters and the unavailable message in other languages. A reply still in the wrong language after one retry gets the unavailable message in the visitor's language and never hands the chat off by itself (the failures-in-a-row handoff still counts it). An answer may come as several messages (on lines of three dashes, up to the setting), and with the setting a table becomes a message of its own. By default AI replies carry the AI assistant label. With Never say it is a bot, the label is hidden and an answer holding one of the setting's Phrases that say it is a bot (whole words; add those of each language your AI answers in) is asked again once, then refused.
knowledge: The knowledge base holds FAQ entries and articles, each in your own collection (such as Shipping or Returns: filter the list with ?collection=, list them with GET /v1/knowledge/collections) and with its language (a code such as en, or empty for any: with Language lock the AI uses only the entries in the visitor's language or in any language); website pages are fetched when you add them and when you press Fetch again, never on a schedule. A page that could not be fetched keeps status failed with its reason: http_status (with the httpStatus the page answered) or unreachable; error says the same in English for people. Edit them in the knowledge editor widget or with the server API.
tools: Webhook tools are defined in Settings → Tools (name, description, typed parameters, https URL, and whether to send the signed-in visitor's id and email). The AI may call them; Chat sends each call as a POST with a JSON body { tool, arguments, conversationId, visitor? } and the header ss-chat-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>"> made with your tool signing secret (Settings → Tools: reveal, copy, regenerate). Calls time out after 8 seconds and at most 64 kB of the answer is read.
booking: Book-a-slot calls your own booking endpoint (Settings → Tools), signed like a tool call, with two requests: { action: "list_slots", from: "YYYY-MM-DD", to: "YYYY-MM-DD", timeZone } answered with { slots: [{ id, start, end }] }, and { action: "book", slotId, name, email, phone, conversationId } answered with { booked: true, reference? }.
handoff: Handoff moves a chat to a person: the visitor asks (button or phrases), a keyword matches, the AI decides, or the AI fails a number of times in a row. The chat is flagged Waiting for a person and the AI stops until a staff member replies or hands the chat back to the AI (resuming the AI: Hand back to the AI in the inbox, or PUT /v1/conversations/<id>/ai with paused false). Outside your office hours the visitor is told when staff are back. A guest with no contact details is asked for them. Reassurance and the queue position count from the latest handoff (waitingSince).
flows: Flows are short scripted step lists (message, question with buttons, collect a field, hand off, end), started by a page rule (the widget starts them when the chat opens on a matching page, or after the delay) or by a keyword in a visitor message. Path patterns start with /: an exact path, * = any characters inside one segment, ** = any segments (for example /products/**).
alerts: Staff alerts, AI cost alerts, transcripts and reply alerts are sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections. They go out with Chat's default words (US English) by email and SMS until you write your own templates in Notifications (Settings → Templates, where you can also switch a message off on a channel); WhatsApp has no default words, so it needs your WhatsApp template approved at Meta. Staff alerts and cost alerts go to the recipients setting (email addresses get email; phone numbers SMS, or WhatsApp with the setting Phones get) and, with the setting Also alert Accounts staff who can, to every unblocked Accounts user whose role may reply in the inbox (inbox.reply) or, with all_staff, may see the inbox (inbox.read) (Accounts token); new message and Chat needs you alerts also go to the assigned person; a message Notifications did not take is tried again on the website's next uses for up to a day. Transcripts are emails; without the token they answer notifications_not_connected. Reply alerts go when staff reply to a visitor who has not checked the chat for the away time (0: also while they are in it): with How often once (the default) one alert until they check again, with every_reply one for each staff reply while they are away; by the setting Channels, in order (email, SMS and WhatsApp; with none picked, the default, the channels switched on in Notifications: email, then SMS, then WhatsApp): the first channel the visitor has an address for (a phone for SMS and WhatsApp), and when Notifications does not take it there (that channel is off, has no template or is switched off for the message), the next one. To send no reply alerts, switch Reply alerts to visitors off. Alerts link to the setting Conversation page in your admin (adminUrl) with its values filled in, for example https://admin.example.com/inbox?conversation={conversationId}; the inbox widget opens the conversation named by ?conversation= in its page address. Staff alert values: visitor, name, preview (140 characters on one line), message (the visitor's latest message, up to 500 characters with its line breaks), phone (with the setting Alerts carry the visitor's phone), link, conversationId and business. A transcript carries the whole chat in {transcript}, a long value of up to 50,000 characters (your own template of chat.transcript uses it in the message, not the subject); a longer chat sends its latest messages after a line that says how many (widget text transcript.earlier).
attachments: Attachments go from the browser straight to your own S3-compatible storage with a short presigned PUT that fixes the type and size; Chat keeps only the object key. Allow your website's origin (and your admin's) in the bucket's CORS: methods PUT and GET, header content-type. Images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF) show inline; PDFs are downloads, or open in a new tab with the setting Open PDFs in the browser. Visitors may send only those (with the setting Visitors may attach: everyone, or signed-in visitors only); staff may also send Word, Excel and text files, always as downloads. Attachment links are Chat's own (/v1/files/…): each use sends the browser on to a fresh 10-minute link in your storage, so the links of a chat left open keep working. The largest file is a setting: for visitors default 5 MB, at most 10 MB; for staff default 10 MB, at most 100 MB.
dataRights: Data rights: paste this website's Chat server token into Accounts. Export returns a person's conversations (with their messages and attachments' names) and leads; delete removes them, guest chats merged into the account included. Chat never deletes conversations because of their age; you delete them with DELETE /v1/conversations/<id>, or every one (your test chats before going live) with POST /v1/data/delete-all { scope: conversations, confirm: '<your domain>' } and the server token: their messages, attachments, guest records and staff alerts not sent yet go with them, leads stay; every lead with { scope: leads, confirm: '<your domain>' }; when the answer says more, call again.
activity: Activity log: every staff action through the widgets or the server API (reply, note, status, assignment, knowledge edits …) is kept in your database and copied to Accounts when its token is pasted: who (with their role), what, the target with its label (the visitor's name, an entry's or saved reply's title), a short detail such as Status: open → resolved, and when — never message contents. Read it with GET /v1/activity (below).
kit: In Chat: the lists of GET and PUT /v1/lists/<list> are tools (Webhook tools), flows (Flows), custom_fields (Custom fields), page_rules (Page rules), fallback_answers (Fallback answers), redaction_patterns (Redaction patterns, each { name, pattern, replacement }) and teams (Teams, each { name, members, languages, pages }), each the whole list in { value }, checked as in Settings. Conversations count with GET /v1/conversations/count and GET /v1/conversations/counts?by=status|waiting|guest|unread, with the list's own filters (status, waiting=1, visitor=guest|user, assigned=unassigned|me, q); waiting, guest (the visitor is a guest) and unread (visitor messages no one on your staff opened) count as true and false. The inbox widget's twins are GET /v1/admin/conversations/count and /counts (inbox.read). Replies, status changes, assignment and knowledge edits made with the server token and SS-Actor headers carry that person's name (on the message, as staffId and name, and in the activity log with their role), add them to the staff list, and assigned=me means them; without the headers they carry no name (the widget, transcripts and reply alerts show your widget text chat.staff) and the activity log names Server. A visitor call from your server sends the guest's key in SS-Guest or the visitor's sign-in in SS-Sign-In, and SS-Visitor-IP: the AI reply limits per network count by that address.
shop: Shop tools, track shipment and product cards read your shop in Ecommerce: paste this website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. Each tool is offered to the AI only while its feature is on: Shop tools: product search and details (search_catalog, get_product_details), deals and savings quotes (quote_product_savings, list_active_deals), top and new products (get_top_products), my orders and account (get_my_orders, get_my_account) and Track-shipment (track_shipment). My orders, account and track shipment are offered only to a visitor whose Accounts sign-in Chat verified on that request; Chat forwards that sign-in to Ecommerce in the SS-Sign-In header, and Ecommerce verifies it itself and answers only that user's data (never full street addresses or phone numbers). The AI never chooses the user, the website or the token. Prices are the ones your product pages show: after the best live deal on one unit, with the earlier price shown struck through and the deal's name and saving, so the AI and the cards never name another price. When Ecommerce cannot answer (token missing or refused, Ecommerce stopped or unreachable), the AI says it cannot look this up right now and everything else keeps working. These are the Ecommerce routes Chat calls with the pasted token (server token; Ecommerce implements exactly these):
install: Add the script to the pages of your website. The chat widget mounts itself; it renders nothing while Visitor chat is off, the product is stopped, or your database is not connected.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: Inbox (inbox.read to see conversations and set your presence, inbox.reply to reply and attach, inbox.manage for status, assignment, notes, saved replies, custom field values and max chats), Knowledge editor (knowledge.edit) and Reports (reports.read). The inbox setting Guest chats in the inbox shows every chat, guest chats only once handed to a person, or signed-in visitors' chats only (in the list, its counts and the unread badge); pausing the AI needs inbox.manage, or inbox.reply with the setting Pausing the AI needs. Staff may say why they pause the AI, and the inbox shows who paused it, when and why; Hand back to the AI resumes the AI in a chat waiting for a person. Delete removes a conversation for good (inbox.manage, asked twice), a visitor's phone shows a Call link, and older messages load a page at a time. A chat can be assigned to anyone on the staff list: everyone the inbox has seen and, with the Accounts token, every Accounts user whose role may reply in the inbox; staff alerts reach the assigned person's email and, from Accounts, their phone; with Assign automatically set to first replier, an unassigned chat goes to the first member of staff who replies. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time. SSChat.onUnread(callback) gives the unread count for your own menu; the server can read it with GET /v1/inbox/unread.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every API route answers JSON (204: no body); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off. The reference below says what each call takes and answers.
cards: Product cards: the products search_catalog, get_product_details and get_top_products return (up to the setting Products per search: default 5, at most 12) show under the AI answer as cards with the image, the name linking to the product page, the price as the product page shows it (after the best live deal, with the earlier price struck through beside it; screen readers hear "was" and that price) and Add to cart. Add to cart dispatches the cancelable window event ss-ecommerce:add-to-cart with detail { productId, variantId, quantity: 1 }. Ecommerce's widget on the same page adds the item to its cart and calls preventDefault(); when no widget does, the card opens the product page instead. Your own cart can listen for the same event. Every word on a card is a widget text (Settings, Texts).
contextPanel: Context panel shop info: with the Ecommerce token pasted and a signed-in visitor, the inbox's context panel also shows the visitor's latest orders (number, status, total; as many as the setting Orders shown: default 5, at most 20) and loyalty points, read from Ecommerce with the server token; for guests, or without the token, it shows nothing about the shop.
import: Import (server token only, feature Import): move staff, guests, conversations and their messages in from another system with ss-import, or with your own script on the import routes. POST /v1/import/<collection> takes NDJSON (application/x-ndjson, one record per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB per call) in Chat's own shapes: staff { id, name, email?, presence?, maxChats?, createdAt? }; guests { keyHash, id, expireAt?, createdAt? }, where keyHash is the SHA-256 (hex) of the old guest cookie value, so a guest's chats keep working through the store's own cookie sent as SS-Guest; conversations with their given ids (visitor, contact, status, waiting, AI pause, assignment, note, custom field values, summary, rating, the page it started on, unread counts, lastMessageAt, createdAt); and messages { id, conversationId, author, staffId?, name?, text, format?, internal?, attachment?, createdAt }, one record per message, after their conversations. Times are ISO 8601 with a zone. Each record is written by its key and replaced when it is there already, so a re-run gives exactly the source again; unknown fields and the tenant fields are refused by name, and text longer than Chat keeps is refused, never cut. ?dryRun=1 checks without writing. Then call POST /v1/import/finish (again with ?after=<next> while more is true): it numbers each imported conversation's messages 1..n by time and derives its counters, preview and read marks. POST /v1/import/<collection>/prune removes imported records the source no longer has (records made in Chat itself stay), and GET /v1/import/status answers the counts and the sums ss-import verify compares. An import sends nothing: no message, event, alert, AI call or activity copy.

build.visitor_chat: Add the widget script with your browser token to every page (copy it from Install and tokens in the Portal); the chat mounts itself, so there is nothing to place. Optionally use window.SSChat: setPage({ kind, productId, productName }) on product, category, deals and cart pages, open() and close(), and onUnread(callback) for your own badge. For your own chat screens instead, use the visitor API with the browser token: GET /v1/chat, POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 and GET /v1/chat/unread.
build.guest_chat: Nothing on your pages: the widget keeps each guest's key on the device. On your own chat screens, keep the guestKey of the first answer in localStorage, send it in the SS-Guest header of every visitor request, and save a guest's contact details with POST /v1/chat/contact.
build.signed_in_chat: Paste your website's Accounts server token into Connections. On every page, pass the visitor's Accounts sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(signIn) (for example from window.SSAccounts.getSignIn()) and call SSChat.identify(null) on sign-out; on your own chat screens, send it in the SS-Sign-In header. Set Sign-in page URL (Settings → Guests) to your sign-in page, where Sign in to continue leads.
build.ai_replies: Nothing on your pages: the chat widget shows the AI replies. Save your AI provider in Connections (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible service, with its key and model). On your own chat screens, send with POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 and, while aiPending is true, check GET /v1/chat?after=<seq> every 3 seconds.
build.ai_backup: Nothing on your pages: save a second AI provider in Connections (Backup AI provider). It answers when the main provider fails.
build.ai_instructions: Nothing on your pages: write your instructions for the AI (up to 32,000 characters) in Settings → Assistant, or save them from your server with PUT /v1/settings/ai_instructions.instructions { value }.
build.fallback_answers: Nothing on your pages: write your answers in Settings → Assistant (Fallback answers), or save them from your server with PUT /v1/lists/fallback_answers { value }, each { language, keywords, text }; a text may hold {deals_table}, {top_products}, {products_under}, {my_orders} or {comparison}, filled from the shop tools that are on (an answer whose placeholder cannot be filled is skipped). {products_under} needs keywords, the words before a budget (under 15,000); the setting Budget words adds words such as k = 1000. {comparison} needs keywords: the words between two products, such as vs; for a message like Lamp Max vs Lamp Mini, each side is looked up in your catalog (with fewer of its words when nothing matches) and the answer shows both side by side in a table: price (with the was price), availability, brand and condition, and their options and specs, in the words of your widget texts.
build.ai_caps: Nothing on your pages: set the daily and monthly AI token caps in Settings → Assistant (days count in your business.json time zone). At a cap the AI stops until the window resets; visitors then get your fallback answers, else what When the AI cannot answer says.
build.ai_cost_alerts: Nothing on your pages: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections, set the share of the monthly cap in Settings → Assistant and list the alert recipients in Settings → Inbox (Alert recipients). The alert goes to them once a month.
build.language_lock: Nothing on your pages: in Settings → Assistant, list the languages the AI may answer in and the default language, and write the unavailable message in your other languages. The AI then answers in the visitor's language.
build.knowledge_base: Nothing on your pages: add FAQ entries and articles in the knowledge editor widget (Knowledge editor) or from your server with POST /v1/knowledge/entries. The AI answers from them.
build.knowledge_pages: Nothing to change on your pages, as long as they are public https pages: add the addresses of the pages the AI should know (shipping, returns, contact …) in the knowledge editor widget or with POST /v1/knowledge/pages. Chat reads a page when you add it and again only with Fetch again (POST /v1/knowledge/pages/<id>/fetch), so fetch it again after you change it.
build.knowledge_editor:
In your admin, place
with the widget script (without data-token) and SSChat.admin({ getTicket }). Your server checks the user's sign-in and role, then asks for a ticket with POST /v1/tickets (server token) carrying knowledge.edit.
build.webhook_tools: On your server, an https endpoint for each tool: Chat POSTs { tool, arguments, conversationId, visitor? } with the ss-chat-signature header. Check it with your tool signing secret (Settings → Tools; the check is in this guide) and answer with a 2xx (JSON or text) within 8 seconds, without redirects (at most 64 kB is read). Define the tools (name, description, typed parameters, address) in Settings → Tools or with PUT /v1/lists/tools { value }.
build.book_slot: On your server, a booking endpoint (https), signed like a tool call (check ss-chat-signature with your tool signing secret): it answers { action: "list_slots", from, to, timeZone } with { slots: [{ id, start, end }] } and { action: "book", slotId, name, email, phone, conversationId } with { booked: true, reference? }. Put its address in Settings → Tools (Booking endpoint).
build.shop_search: Nothing on your pages: paste your website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. The AI then searches your catalog and reads product details through Ecommerce.
build.shop_deals: Nothing on your pages: paste your website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. The AI then lists your active deals (as many as the setting Deals per list: default 10, at most 20) and quotes a product's price after them.
build.shop_top: Nothing on your pages: paste your website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. The AI then shows your best-selling and newest products (as many as the setting Products per list: default 5, at most 12).
build.shop_my_orders: Paste your website's Ecommerce and Accounts server tokens into Connections, and pass each signed-in visitor's Accounts sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(signIn) (Signed-in chat; on your own chat screens, the SS-Sign-In header). The AI then tells only that visitor about their own orders (the latest, as many as the setting Orders per answer: default 5, at most 10), loyalty points and name.
build.track_shipment: Paste your website's Ecommerce and Accounts server tokens into Connections, and pass each signed-in visitor's Accounts sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(signIn) (Signed-in chat; on your own chat screens, the SS-Sign-In header). The AI then gives only that visitor the courier, tracking number, tracking link and latest status of their own orders.
build.product_cards: Paste your website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. With Ecommerce's widget on the same page, Add to cart adds the item; for your own cart, listen for the window event ss-ecommerce:add-to-cart (detail { productId, variantId, quantity }), add the item and call preventDefault(). When nobody does, the card opens the product page. On your own chat screens, show each card's price with its compareAtPrice (when not null) struck through beside it, as the product page does.
build.shop_context: Paste your website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. On product pages, call SSChat.setPage({ kind: 'product', productId, productName }) (on your own chat screens, send page with each message) so the AI knows the product the visitor is viewing. The setting Longest store information cuts what the AI gets (default and most 6,000 characters; shorter costs fewer AI tokens).
build.proactive_idle: Nothing beyond the widget script: in Settings → Proactive, set the idle minutes, your nudge text for product, category, deals and cart pages (empty = the general text in Texts), once per visit or once per product, and whether phones get none. Call SSChat.setPage({ kind, productId, productName }) on those pages (kind product, category, deals or cart) so the nudge uses that page's text and names the product.
build.proactive_pages: Nothing beyond the widget script: add page rules (a path pattern such as /products/**, a delay and a message) in Settings → Proactive, or with PUT /v1/lists/page_rules { value }.
build.proactive_exit: Nothing beyond the widget script: on desktop, the widget shows the exit message when the pointer leaves the top of the window. Change its words in Settings → Texts.
build.leads_flows: Nothing beyond the widget script: choose the lead fields and the consent text in Settings → Lead capture, and build flows in Settings → Flows or with PUT /v1/lists/flows { value }. The lead form shows at the guest limit and, outside office hours (Human handoff), to a guest who left no email or phone (on your own chat screens: leadOffered in the chat answer). Read leads from your server with GET /v1/leads (your staff see them in the inbox's Leads), and delete one with DELETE /v1/leads/<id> (Delete in the inbox, inbox.manage). On your own chat screens, use POST /v1/chat/leads, POST /v1/chat/flows/<flowId>/start and POST /v1/chat/flow.
build.custom_fields: Nothing on your pages: define the fields in Settings → Custom fields or with PUT /v1/lists/custom_fields { value }. Flows and the lead form can ask for them; your staff set them in the inbox, and your server with PATCH /v1/conversations/<id>.
build.attachments: Connect your S3-compatible storage in Connections and allow your website's origin (and your admin's) in the bucket's CORS: methods PUT and GET, header content-type. The widget uploads by itself; on your own chat screens, ask for an upload with POST /v1/chat/uploads, PUT the file to the address it answers with exactly its headers, then send the attachment with POST /v1/chat/messages.
build.typing_receipts: Nothing on your pages: the widget shows typing and Seen. On your own chat screens, show typing while aiPending is true and mark replies seen with POST /v1/chat/read.
build.ratings: Nothing on your pages: the widget asks for a rating as Settings → Ratings says: satisfaction (csat) with your own label per point, lowest first (2 to 10, for example Bad and Good), or the Net Promoter Score (nps, 0 to 10, its words in your widget texts); reports show the csat average and the NPS. On your own chat screens, send it with POST /v1/chat/rating; your staff ask in the inbox, your server with POST /v1/conversations/<id>/rating-request.
build.transcripts: Paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections. Visitors ask for a copy in the widget (on your own chat screens, POST /v1/chat/transcript), your staff in the inbox, and your server with POST /v1/conversations/<id>/transcript.
build.inbox:
In your admin, place
with the widget script (without data-token) and SSChat.admin({ getTicket }). Your server checks the user's sign-in and role, then asks for a ticket with POST /v1/tickets (server token) carrying inbox.read, inbox.reply and inbox.manage as the role allows. Or work from your server with GET /v1/conversations and POST /v1/conversations//messages.
build.handoff: Nothing on your pages: the widget shows the Talk to a person button and the handoff notice (the widget text chat.handoffNotice, or none with the setting off). Set the phrases (in each language your visitors write in), keywords and office hours in Settings → Handoff and office hours, and keep someone answering in the inbox. On your own chat screens, call POST /v1/chat/handoff when the visitor asks for a person.
build.assignment: Nothing on your pages: your staff assign chats in the inbox (inbox.manage), and your server with PATCH /v1/conversations/<id>. With the Accounts token pasted, anyone whose role may reply in the inbox can be assigned. With Assign automatically round robin or least busy, a chat that comes to your staff (handed to a person, or any chat while AI replies are off) goes to an online member with room: of the first team in Settings → Inbox (Teams) whose languages hold the visitor's language (Language lock) or whose pages match the page, else of the team with neither, else of all your staff; round robin picks the one who got a chat the longest ago, least busy the fewest open chats.
build.presence_queue: Nothing on your pages: your staff set Online, Away or Offline in the inbox. Set the default max chats per person and whether visitors see their place in line in Settings → Handoff and office hours.
build.internal_notes: Nothing on your pages: your staff add notes in the inbox (inbox.manage), and your server with POST /v1/conversations/<id>/notes, or PUT /v1/conversations/<id>/note when notes are one note per chat (Settings → Other settings).
build.saved_replies: Nothing on your pages: your staff save and reuse replies in the inbox widget; saving, changing or deleting one needs inbox.manage.
build.context_panel: Nothing on your pages: the inbox shows who the visitor is, where the chat started and their earlier chats. With your website's Ecommerce server token in Connections, it also shows a signed-in visitor's last orders and loyalty points.
build.ai_summary: Nothing on your pages: the AI writes a summary when a chat is handed to a person; your staff ask for one in the inbox, and your server with POST /v1/conversations/<id>/summary. The setting Summary instructions says what it holds, how long it is and its language; a summary never adds anything that is not in the chat.
build.staff_alerts: Paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections, and set Conversation page in your admin (the admin page with your inbox widget, with {conversationId}) and the alert recipients in Settings → Inbox. Email and SMS go out with Chat's default words; WhatsApp needs your own template approved at Meta (Notifications, Settings → Templates).
build.visitor_alerts: Paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections and pick the channels, in order, and how often in Settings → Other settings. A visitor gets an alert only at an address Chat has: the email or phone of their Accounts sign-in, or the contact details they left.
build.moderation: Nothing on your pages: in Settings → Moderation, choose whether personal data is hidden (cards, IBANs, emails, phones, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses), your own redaction patterns (national or tax IDs, member numbers: a safe subset of regular expressions, checked when saved, that can never slow the chat down), your blocked terms, the link policy for AI answers and the phrases the AI must never reveal.
build.reports:
In your admin, place
with the widget script (without data-token) and SSChat.admin({ getTicket }), with tickets carrying reports.read; or read GET /v1/reports from your server.
build.import: Nothing on your pages. While Import is on (our admins switch it on for a move and off after it), run ss-import, or your own script with the server token: POST /v1/import/<collection> with NDJSON (staff, guests, conversations, then messages), then POST /v1/import/finish, and compare GET /v1/import/status.
